name: The full case (document)
thesis: Edo read whole as the earliest documentable mass creative industry: one essential question, a system diagram, a cast of 58, six eras, 52 objects, eight lectures and ten interactives, as a reference recipe for every F1 page.
judged: No critique of the document itself is recorded. It was written because the lead judged the existing reference pages "still pretty weak, from concept to execution" (research/edo-2026-10-04/README.md), and it is the yardstick later critiques use (REPORT_EDO_REDESIGN.md cites its ~62-minute lecture plan and notes v2 dropped three of its ten interactives).

spine.label: System-first reference document
spine.desc: Sections run concept → cast by role → six-era spine → object set → lectures → interactives → how it holds together (EDO_FULL_CASE.md §1–§7), organised around the essential question "How does a city turn pictures into a mass market, and who gets named when it does?" and a five-part system (inputs, four trades, market, afterlife).

layout.label: Long-form doc, tables
layout.desc: A single-column Claude Doc with ~114 table rows (cast, eras, events); no screens or stage (EDO_FULL_CASE.md).

navigation.label: Numbered headings only
navigation.desc: Ten numbered sections; no in-page wayfinding beyond the doc outline.

questioning.label: Specified predictions and checks
questioning.desc: Each lecture specifies one "Prediction (one tap on the map)" and an "Argued" station; each interactive ends on a one-tap "Check" (EDO_FULL_CASE.md §5–§6). Nothing is built.

tools.label: Ten designed interactives (I1–I10)
tools.desc: Read the margin, Peel the colours, One design many originals, The city 1677–1859, What a sheet cost, The blue route, Before and after the ban, An edition, The export map, The contract; each with lens, data, what the learner does, what it shows, check (§6).

visual.label: Plain document
visual.desc: Doc typography plus one embedded system-diagram widget that the repo export only records as "[embedded content: the system of the floating world …]".

text.label: Dense, sourced reference prose
text.desc: 8,753 words; confidence words on claims, quotes ≤ 25 words, Japanese name order, content-note protocol (§8).

people.label: Cast tables by role
people.desc: Publishers, designers by school, carvers and printers (three named), censors and the state, theatre, dealers and collectors; 58 documented, 46 named; the publisher first because the 1790 law named him (§2).

mapping.label: None built (maps specified)
mapping.desc: Maps exist only as specifications: I4 1677↔1859 LoC transparency, I6 blue-route arcs, I9 export map (§6).

timeline.label: Era table + anchor-event list
timeline.desc: Six eras (A city is made … The afterlife) each "turned by something a learner can date", plus 78 sourced events (§3).

layout.label: Separate screens (artboards)
layout.desc: canvas.json lays out six 1440-wide boards: a long case page (1440×3560), a lecture player (dark stage + 8-station sidebar), and one page per interactive.

navigation.label: Hub page + lens bar + station list
navigation.desc: Top bar lens pills (Time, Place, Movements, Objects); lecture player with numbered station list and Previous/Next station plus a progress bar (Lecture.dc.html); every screen links "← Edo Japan · case".

tools.label: Standalone interactive pages (3 of 10 built)
tools.desc: Margin.dc.html: five hotspots on Hiroshige's Sudden Shower, then date the sheet to a censor band; Ban.dc.html: year scrubber 1835–1850 fading genres; Cost.dc.html: price bars against a bowl of soba with the 1842 cap line.

motion.label: Static state swaps
motion.desc: DCLogic setState re-renders only; no timers, transitions or scroll-linked motion in any artboard script.

text.label: Short station narration with claim ids
text.desc: "Narration · every factual sentence carries its claim id": one or two sentences per station (Lecture.dc.html); the case page carries thesis, stats and card blurbs. Judged "lectures too thin".

people.label: Role tabs over dark text cards
people.desc: Main.dc.html "The organiser first": five role tabs (Publishers 8, Designers 20, Carvers and printers, Censors and the state, Dealers and collectors); name + kanji + dates + note, no portraits.

mapping.label: Schematic place diagram
mapping.desc: Atlas.dc.html Place lens: labelled pills in a Japan box and a world box with arc counts; the board notes "The live build is MapLibre on OpenHistoricalMap tiles". No geography drawn.

timeline.label: Proportional era bands + event chips
timeline.desc: Atlas.dc.html Time lens: six eras with widths proportional to years (afterlife folded), 12 dated event chips; tapping one opens a node card shared by every lens.

name: The scrolling atlas
thesis: One continuous scroll in place of the artboards: a Pacific-centred world map and a proportional timeline animate beside six chapters, with eight tools embedded where the story needs them.
judged: not coherent; tools primitive; atlas should be an interactive world map; timeline should be designed like one with animations; elements need visuals; lazy. (Research critique: "a well-sourced essay with a slideshow of dots beside it" — REPORT_EDO_REDESIGN.md.)
